samples.question: The picture shows one rectangular plate on white paper. Black walls divide the plate into regions; each region is a single connected area of one flat colour, and every wall inside the plate separates two different regions. Exactly one region is filled red and exactly one other region is filled blue; all remaining regions are white. Two regions count as NEIGHBOURS only if they are separated by a wall along a whole stretch of their border; regions that meet only where walls cross, at a single corner point, are NOT neighbours. The white paper outside the plate and the black walls themselves are not regions. Which shaded region has more neighbours: the red region, the blue region, or do they have the same number? Answer red, blue, or same.
